questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Gate or boom across the road ahead

questions.explanation: Gate (W314): a gate or boom across the road ahead; be prepared to stop.
questions.manualRef: NaTIS Learner Driver Manual – Road Traffic Signs §4.3 W314 (p.28)

questions.question: Which sign means: "No overtaking for the next 500 m"?
questions.explanation: Overtaking prohibited (R214): do not overtake any vehicle for the next 500 m.
questions.manualRef: NaTIS Learner Driver Manual – Road Traffic Signs §3.3 R214 (p.12)

questions.question: What does this sign indicate?

options.text: Staggered junction: side road from the left first, then from the right
Staggered junction: side road from the right first, then from the left

questions.explanation: Staggered junction (W109): a road joins from the right first and then, a short distance on, from the left.
questions.manualRef: NaTIS Learner Driver Manual – Road Traffic Signs §4.1 W109 (p.24)

questions.question: When should you let go of the ignition key while starting the engine?

options.text: As soon as the engine starts

questions.explanation: Release hold on the key as soon as the engine starts.
questions.manualRef: NaTIS K53 Light Motor Vehicle (Code B) manual, Module 3 (p.19)

questions.question: What is the meaning of this sign?

options.text: Stop – but you may turn left without stopping if you yield to traffic
Pedestrian priority area (max 15 km/h for permitted vehicles)
3-way stop: the vehicle that stopped first moves off first

questions.explanation: 3-way stop (R1.3): traffic from all three directions must stop; the vehicle that stopped first should move off first.
questions.manualRef: NaTIS Learner Driver Manual – Road Traffic Signs §3.1 R1.3 (p.4)

questions.question: A motorcycle may be fitted with a retreaded tyre.
questions.explanation: You may not ride a motorcycle equipped with a retreaded tyre.
questions.manualRef: NaTIS Learner Driver Manual – Rules of the Road §6.61 (p.37)

questions.question: In this automatic-transmission car, what is control number 4?
questions.explanation: Control 4 is the steering wheel.
questions.manualRef: NaTIS Learner Driver Manual – Vehicle Controls §2.3–2.5 Light motor vehicle – automatic gearbox (p.9–10)

questions.question: In this manual-transmission car, what is control number 7?
questions.explanation: Control 7 is the hand brake (parking brake).
questions.manualRef: NaTIS Learner Driver Manual – Vehicle Controls §2.1–2.2 Light motor vehicle – manual gearbox (p.8–9)

questions.question: In this automatic car, which control is used to slow down or stop?
questions.explanation: Control 9 is the brake.
questions.manualRef: NaTIS Learner Driver Manual – Vehicle Controls §2.3–2.5 Light motor vehicle – automatic gearbox (p.9–10); NaTIS Learner Driver Manual – Vehicle Controls §2.6 Sample questions (p.11)

questions.question: Put these steps for changing up a gear in an automatic car (manual selection) in the correct order.
questions.explanation: LMV Module 25.
questions.manualRef: NaTIS K53 Light Motor Vehicle (Code B) manual, Module 25 (p.46)

questions.question: What is a "professional driver"?

options.text: The driver of a motor vehicle of a prescribed class that requires a professional driving permit
Any driver who has had a licence for 5 years

questions.explanation: "Professional driver" means the driver of a motor vehicle of a prescribed class (requiring a professional driving permit).
questions.manualRef: NaTIS Learner Driver Manual – Rules of the Road – Acronyms and definitions (p.7)

questions.question: Which vehicles are prohibited from entering the area marked by this sign, except for local access or delivery? (Select all that apply.)

options.text: Vehicles with a mass exceeding 3 500 kg

questions.explanation: Woonerf (R403): prohibits vehicles over 3 500 kg or with more than 10 seats, except for local access or delivery.
questions.manualRef: NaTIS Learner Driver Manual – Road Traffic Signs §3.5 R403 (p.19)

questions.question: At a speed hump marking you should slow down and release your brake before driving over the hump.
questions.explanation: Speed hump (WM10): slow down and release your brake before driving over the speed hump.
questions.manualRef: NaTIS Learner Driver Manual – Road Traffic Signs §7.2 WM10 (p.53)

questions.question: Put these steps for moving off in an automatic car in the correct order.

options.text: Check rear-view mirror(s) and blind spot

questions.explanation: LMV Module 13 (moving off, automatic transmission).
questions.manualRef: NaTIS K53 Light Motor Vehicle (Code B) manual, Module 13 (p.29)

questions.question: Sign R214 prohibits overtaking for the next ____.
questions.explanation: Overtaking prohibited (R214): do not overtake any vehicle for the next 500 m.
questions.manualRef: NaTIS Learner Driver Manual – Road Traffic Signs §3.3 R214 (p.12)

questions.question: Link each regulatory sign with its correct meaning.
questions.explanation: Sign 1 is R101: Minimum speed 50 km/h. Sign 2 is R106: Proceed right only. Sign 3 is R119: Minibuses only. Sign 4 is R111: Cyclists only.
questions.manualRef: NaTIS Learner Driver Manual – Road Traffic Signs R101 (p.6), R106 (p.6), R119 (p.7), R111 (p.6)

questions.question: Match each warning sign shown to what it means.

options.text: Combined curves: first sharp curve to the left
Combined curves: first sharp curve to the right

questions.explanation: Sign 1 is W211: Combined curves: first sharp curve to the left. Sign 2 is W210: Combined curves: first sharp curve to the right. Sign 3 is W201: Traffic circle ahead. Sign 4 is W204: Sharp curve to the right.
questions.manualRef: NaTIS Learner Driver Manual – Road Traffic Signs W211 (p.25), W210 (p.25), W201 (p.25), W204 (p.25)

questions.question: You may drive at night with only the parking lamps switched on if the street lights are on.
questions.explanation: Never drive a vehicle with only the parking lamps switched on.
questions.manualRef: NaTIS Learner Driver Manual – Rules of the Road §6.4 (p.17)

questions.question: Which vehicle needs number plates at both the front and the rear?
questions.explanation: Motorcycles, motor tricycles and trailers have a rear plate only; all other motor vehicles front and rear.
questions.manualRef: NaTIS Learner Driver Manual – Rules of the Road §6.8 (p.17)

questions.question: What does this sign indicate?

options.text: 4-way stop: the vehicle that stopped first moves off first

questions.explanation: Yield to oncoming traffic (R6): a single carriageway ahead is used by vehicles from both directions; yield to vehicles already in it.
questions.manualRef: NaTIS Learner Driver Manual – Road Traffic Signs §3.1 R6 (p.5)

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Right turn prohibited (you may go straight or turn left)

questions.explanation: Motor cars prohibited (R223): do not enter if you are driving a motor car.
questions.manualRef: NaTIS Learner Driver Manual – Road Traffic Signs §3.3 R223 (p.13)

questions.question: Tap the sign that means: "Pay and display: pay the parking fee and display the receipt".
questions.explanation: Pay and display (R523): pay the parking fee and display the receipt on or in your vehicle.
questions.manualRef: NaTIS Learner Driver Manual – Road Traffic Signs §3.6 R523 (p.20)

questions.question: Who may steer a vehicle that is being towed?

options.text: Nobody – the steering must be locked
A person holding a driving licence for that class of vehicle

questions.explanation: The steering of a towed vehicle must be controlled by a person holding a licence for that class of vehicle.
questions.manualRef: NaTIS Learner Driver Manual – Rules of the Road §6.57 (p.36)

questions.question: How should the exterior (side) mirrors be adjusted?

options.text: Pointing at the road surface next to the car
So that a small portion of the rear-most part of the vehicle body is visible on the inner side of the mirror
So that you can see the rear wheels clearly
Pointing straight out to the side

questions.explanation: Exterior mirrors shall be adjusted so that a small portion of the rear-most part of the body is visible in the inner side of the mirror.
questions.manualRef: NaTIS K53 Light Motor Vehicle (Code B) manual, Glossary – Maximum rear-view vision (p.82)

questions.question: What is the "edge of the roadway" on a tarred road if it is not marked by a sign?

options.text: The outer edge of the shoulder
The edge of the bituminous or concrete surface

questions.explanation: In the absence of a sign, on a bituminous or concrete surface road the edge of the roadway is the edge of that surface.
questions.manualRef: NaTIS Learner Driver Manual – Rules of the Road – Acronyms and definitions (p.3)

questions.question: What is the best way to carry baggage on a motorcycle?

options.text: In suitable carriers securely attached to the motorcycle

questions.explanation: The best way to transport baggage on a motorcycle is in suitable carriers attached securely to the motorcycle.
questions.manualRef: NaTIS Learner Driver Manual – Rules of the Road §6.33 (p.25)

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Side road junction from the right

questions.explanation: Y-junction (W115): the road forks into two; decide in time which road to take.
questions.manualRef: NaTIS Learner Driver Manual – Road Traffic Signs §4.1 W115 (p.24)

questions.question: Which control is used before applying the brake in order to slow down or stop?
questions.explanation: The centre rear-view mirror (1) – check what is behind you before braking.
questions.manualRef: NaTIS Learner Driver Manual – Vehicle Controls §2.6 Sample questions (p.11)

questions.question: A combination is a heavy motor vehicle combination if the GVM of the trailer exceeds ____.
questions.explanation: HMV includes combinations of vehicles of which the GVM of the trailer exceeds 750 kg.
questions.manualRef: NaTIS Learner Driver Manual – Rules of the Road – Acronyms and definitions (p.10)

questions.question: Click on the car that is parked illegally.
questions.explanation: No parking on the same side of the road as a fire hydrant within 1,5 m on either side of it. Car B is next to the hydrant.
questions.manualRef: NaTIS Learner Driver Manual – Rules of the Road §6.47 (p.31)

questions.question: Which control is used to avoid the vehicle stalling just before coming to a complete standstill?
questions.explanation: The clutch (8).
questions.manualRef: NaTIS Learner Driver Manual – Vehicle Controls §2.6 Sample questions (p.11)

questions.question: Which sign means: "Temporary STOP/GO control: you may proceed with caution"?
questions.explanation: STOP/RY-GO sign (R1.5), usually at road works: two signs mounted back to back. Stop when STOP is shown; proceed with caution when GO is shown.
questions.manualRef: NaTIS Learner Driver Manual – Road Traffic Signs §3.1 R1.5 (p.4)

questions.question: Which control assists the driver when engaging or disengaging a gear?
questions.explanation: The clutch (8).
questions.manualRef: NaTIS Learner Driver Manual – Vehicle Controls §2.6 Sample questions (p.11)

questions.question: A motor vehicle must be fitted with a speedometer if it can reach what speed?
questions.explanation: A motor vehicle designed for or capable of reaching 60 km/h or more must be fitted with a speedometer.
questions.manualRef: NaTIS Learner Driver Manual – Rules of the Road §6.26 (p.24)

questions.question: This sign means: "Stop – but you may turn left without stopping if you yield to traffic".
questions.explanation: False. Yield to pedestrians (R2.1): give priority to pedestrians crossing or wanting to cross and be ready to stop. ("Stop – but you may turn left without stopping if you yield to traffic" is the meaning of R1.2.)
questions.manualRef: NaTIS Learner Driver Manual – Road Traffic Signs §3.1 R2.1 (p.5)

questions.question: Where would you usually find this sign?

options.text: At the end of a one-way street or of an off-ramp
At the start of a freeway

questions.explanation: No entry (R3) is usually found at the end of a one-way street, at the end of an off-ramp, or where two-way roads change to one-way.
questions.manualRef: NaTIS Learner Driver Manual – Road Traffic Signs §3.1 R3 (p.5)

questions.question: Which sign means: "T-junction chevron: road does not continue straight"?
questions.explanation: T-junction chevron (W409): the road ahead does not carry on straight; slow down to turn or stop.
questions.manualRef: NaTIS Learner Driver Manual – Road Traffic Signs §4.3 W409 (p.34)

questions.question: You are driving on a freeway and notice a vehicle wishing to merge from an on-ramp ahead of you. What must you do?

options.text: Allow it to merge in front of you
Speed up so that it merges behind you

questions.explanation: A driver on a freeway who notices a vehicle wishing to merge from an on-ramp must allow it to merge in front of them.
questions.manualRef: NaTIS Learner Driver Manual – Rules of the Road §6.56 (p.35)

questions.question: What does this sign indicate?

options.text: Reserved for authorised vehicles (e.g. diplomatic corps)

questions.explanation: Authorised vehicle reservation (R324), e.g. diplomatic corps.
questions.manualRef: NaTIS Learner Driver Manual – Road Traffic Signs §3.4 R324 (p.18)

questions.question: What is the meaning of this sign?

options.text: Staggered junction: side road from the left first, then from the right

questions.explanation: Crossroad (W101): approach cautiously and be able to stop if cross-traffic requires it.
questions.manualRef: NaTIS Learner Driver Manual – Road Traffic Signs §4.1 W101 (p.23)

questions.question: How does a heavy-vehicle driver check a 3-second following distance?

options.text: Keep 3 m behind the vehicle ahead
Count to three after the brake lights ahead come on
Count "2001, 2002, 2003" after the vehicle ahead passes a fixed point

questions.explanation: For heavy vehicles, count "2001, 2002, 2003" from when the rear of the vehicle ahead passes a fixed point.
questions.manualRef: NaTIS K53 Heavy Motor Vehicle manual, Glossary – Following distance (p.77); Module 25 (p.44)

questions.question: By definition, a "motorcycle" is a motor vehicle that…

options.text: Has an engine smaller than 125 cm³
Is driven with handlebars, regardless of wheels
Has two wheels, including one with a sidecar attached

questions.explanation: "Motorcycle" means a motor vehicle that has two wheels and includes such a vehicle with a sidecar attached.
questions.manualRef: NaTIS Learner Driver Manual – Rules of the Road – Acronyms and definitions (p.5)

questions.question: When coming to a stop, press the ____ before disengaging the clutch, to prevent coasting.
questions.explanation: The brake pedal shall be depressed before disengaging the clutch to prevent coasting.
questions.manualRef: NaTIS K53 Light Motor Vehicle (Code B) manual, Module 11 (p.27)

questions.question: What is the meaning of this sign?

options.text: Divided path: cyclists on one side, pedestrians on the other

questions.explanation: R113 shows a divided path: cyclists use the part with the bicycle symbol and pedestrians the part with the pedestrian symbol.
questions.manualRef: NaTIS Learner Driver Manual – Road Traffic Signs §3.2 R113 (p.7)

questions.question: When being overtaken on your right on a two-way road, what must you NOT do?
questions.explanation: Do not accelerate whilst being overtaken; increasing speed while being overtaken on a two-way road is a violation of traffic law.
questions.manualRef: NaTIS K53 Light Motor Vehicle (Code B) manual, Module 52 (p.73); NaTIS Learner Driver Manual – Rules of the Road §6.45 (p.29)

questions.question: Which documents must a professional driver keep in the vehicle while driving a vehicle of a prescribed class?

options.text: The driving licence and the professional driving permit

questions.explanation: A licence must be kept in the vehicle (5.2) and a professional driver must keep the professional driving permit in the vehicle (5.7).
questions.manualRef: NaTIS Learner Driver Manual – Rules of the Road §5.2 (p.13); NaTIS Learner Driver Manual – Rules of the Road §5.7 (p.14)

questions.question: What does this sign indicate?

options.text: Winding road (first bend to the right)
Lane ends: the right-hand lane ends
Combined curves: first sharp curve to the right
Combined curves: first sharp curve to the left

questions.explanation: Lane ends (W214): the road narrows by a full lane from the right-hand side; change in good time to the lane that carries on.
questions.manualRef: NaTIS Learner Driver Manual – Road Traffic Signs §4.2 W214 (p.26)

questions.question: What must you do when a vehicle sounding a siren or bell approaches?

options.text: Give it an immediate and absolute right of way
Speed up to stay ahead of it
Continue normally – it must go around you

questions.explanation: You may not fail to give an immediate and absolute right of way to a vehicle sounding a device or bell.
questions.manualRef: NaTIS Learner Driver Manual – Rules of the Road §6.49 (p.32)

questions.question: What is the hand brake (parking brake) used for?

options.text: To advise other road users of your intention to turn or change direction
To increase the speed of the vehicle
To keep the vehicle stationary after parking

questions.explanation: The hand brake (parking brake) is used to keep the vehicle stationary after parking.
questions.manualRef: NaTIS Learner Driver Manual – Vehicle Controls §2.6 Sample questions (p.11)

questions.question: In this automatic car, which control do you use to signal that you are turning?
questions.explanation: Control 5 is the indicator light switch.
questions.manualRef: NaTIS Learner Driver Manual – Vehicle Controls §2.3–2.5 Light motor vehicle – automatic gearbox (p.9–10); NaTIS Learner Driver Manual – Vehicle Controls §2.6 Sample questions (p.11)

questions.question: Which shape is ordinarily used for guidance signs?
questions.explanation: Guidance signs are ordinarily rectangular.
questions.manualRef: NaTIS Learner Driver Manual – Road Traffic Signs §1 Signs in general (p.2)

questions.question: What is the meaning of this sign?
questions.explanation: Gravel road ends (W363): look out for a tar or concrete road ahead.
questions.manualRef: NaTIS Learner Driver Manual – Road Traffic Signs §4.3 W363 (p.33)

questions.question: What is the indicator light switch used for?

options.text: To advise other road users of your intention to turn or change direction
To engage or disengage a gear and to avoid stalling just before stopping
To change the direction of the vehicle (steer left or right)
To keep the vehicle stationary after parking

questions.explanation: The indicator light switch is used to advise other road users of your intention to turn or change direction.
questions.manualRef: NaTIS Learner Driver Manual – Vehicle Controls §2.6 Sample questions (p.11)

questions.question: Checking the pressure on the brake and clutch pedals is part of the interior pre-trip inspection.
questions.explanation: Pre-trip inspection (interior) includes checking pressure on brake and clutch pedals.
questions.manualRef: NaTIS K53 Light Motor Vehicle (Code B) manual, Module 2 (p.18)

questions.question: Tap the sign that means: "Single-carriageway freeway begins".
questions.explanation: Single-carriageway freeway begins (R402): all freeway rules apply from the sign.
questions.manualRef: NaTIS Learner Driver Manual – Road Traffic Signs §3.5 R402 (p.19)

questions.question: What is the meaning of this sign?

options.text: Dead end: turn left or right
Danger plate: do not pass to the right of it
T-junction chevron: road does not continue straight

questions.explanation: T-junction chevron (W409): the road ahead does not carry on straight; slow down to turn or stop.
questions.manualRef: NaTIS Learner Driver Manual – Road Traffic Signs §4.3 W409 (p.34)

questions.question: Look at the picture. Which car is parked illegally?
questions.explanation: Car B is within 1,5 m of the fire hydrant on the same side of the road.
questions.manualRef: NaTIS Learner Driver Manual – Rules of the Road §6.47 (p.31)

questions.question: What is "slipping the clutch"?

options.text: Pressing the clutch to the floor
Holding the clutch at the friction point so that engine power is only partially transmitted to the wheels

questions.explanation: Slipping is holding the clutch at the friction point so engine power is only partially transmitted; it causes abnormal wear.
questions.manualRef: NaTIS K53 Light Motor Vehicle (Code B) manual, Glossary – Clutch – slips (p.80)

questions.question: Which lane ends according to this sign?

options.text: No lane – a lane is added

questions.explanation: Lane ends (W214): the road narrows by a full lane from the right-hand side.
questions.manualRef: NaTIS Learner Driver Manual – Road Traffic Signs §4.2 W214 (p.26)

questions.question: Put these final steps for stopping to park an automatic car in the correct order.

options.text: Check mirrors and blind spots before opening doors
Cancel signal and switch off accessories

questions.explanation: LMV Module 32 (stopping for parking, automatic transmission).
questions.manualRef: NaTIS K53 Light Motor Vehicle (Code B) manual, Module 32 (p.53)

questions.question: What does this road marking mean?
questions.explanation: RM15: drive around the circle only in the direction of the arrows; yield to traffic from the right.
questions.manualRef: NaTIS Learner Driver Manual – Road Traffic Signs §7.1 RM15 (p.52)

questions.question: Which sign means: "Yield to pedestrians"?
questions.explanation: Yield to pedestrians (R2.1): give priority to pedestrians crossing or wanting to cross and be ready to stop.
questions.manualRef: NaTIS Learner Driver Manual – Road Traffic Signs §3.1 R2.1 (p.5)

questions.question: How many independent braking systems must a motorcycle have?

options.text: Two – one for the front wheel and one for the rear

questions.explanation: A motorcycle must have two independent brakes (front and rear).
questions.manualRef: NaTIS Learner Driver Manual – Rules of the Road §6.14.1 (p.19)

questions.question: Which rule applies to driving on a freeway?

options.text: Use any lane and overtake on either side
Drive on the shoulder when traffic is slow
Keep left and overtake on the right
Keep right and overtake on the left

questions.explanation: Vehicles must keep left and overtake to the right on any freeway.
questions.manualRef: NaTIS Learner Driver Manual – Rules of the Road §6.45 (p.29)

questions.question: What does this sign indicate?

options.text: Left turn prohibited (you may go straight or turn right)
Towed vehicles prohibited (no towing beyond this sign)
No overtaking for the next 500 m

questions.explanation: Overtaking prohibited (R214): do not overtake any vehicle for the next 500 m.
questions.manualRef: NaTIS Learner Driver Manual – Road Traffic Signs §3.3 R214 (p.12)

questions.question: How many red retro-reflectors must be fitted at the rear of a light motor vehicle?

options.text: None if it has rear lamps

questions.explanation: A light motor vehicle must be fitted at the rear with two red retro-reflectors, one on each side.
questions.manualRef: NaTIS Learner Driver Manual – Rules of the Road §6.43 (p.29)

questions.question: What must you do when approaching a level crossing?

options.text: Only look if the booms are down
Look to the right and left for rail traffic
Change gear while on the tracks

questions.explanation: On approach to a level crossing, look to the right and left for rail traffic.
questions.manualRef: NaTIS K53 Light Motor Vehicle (Code B) manual, Module 47 (p.68)

questions.question: During the interior pre-trip inspection, which of these must you check? (Select all that apply.)

options.text: Seat adjustment for the correct driving position
Operation of lights, indicators, horn and wipers
All mirrors for maximum rear view

questions.explanation: Interior checks include lights, indicators, horn, wipers, seat adjustment and mirrors (the oil is part of the exterior check).
questions.manualRef: NaTIS K53 Light Motor Vehicle (Code B) manual, Module 2 (p.18)

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Heavy vehicles may not overtake other heavy vehicles (500 m)

questions.explanation: U-turn prohibited (R213): do not turn your vehicle around to face the opposite direction.
questions.manualRef: NaTIS Learner Driver Manual – Road Traffic Signs §3.3 R213 (p.12)

questions.question: Tap the window wiper in this manual-transmission car.
questions.explanation: The window wiper is control 2.
questions.manualRef: NaTIS Learner Driver Manual – Vehicle Controls §2.1–2.2 Light motor vehicle – manual gearbox (p.8–9)

questions.question: You must not drive a vehicle so as to cause excessive noise.
questions.explanation: No person shall operate a vehicle on a public road in a manner causing excessive noise.
questions.manualRef: NaTIS Learner Driver Manual – Rules of the Road §6.25 (p.23)

questions.question: Sign W307 warns that pedestrians may be crossing the road for the next ____.
questions.explanation: Pedestrians (W307): may be crossing the road for the next 2 km.
questions.manualRef: NaTIS Learner Driver Manual – Road Traffic Signs §4.3 W307 (p.27)

questions.question: Goods may be loaded so that they obscure your view in the rear-view mirrors, provided you use the side mirrors.
questions.explanation: Goods may not be loaded in a way that obscures the driver's view to the front or sides, or the view in the rear-view mirror(s).
questions.manualRef: NaTIS Learner Driver Manual – Rules of the Road §6.33 (p.25)

questions.question: On which side of a motorcycle must a sidecar be attached?
questions.explanation: A sidecar must be attached to the left side of the motorcycle.
questions.manualRef: NaTIS Learner Driver Manual – Rules of the Road §6.51 (p.34)

questions.question: What does this signal mean?

options.text: You have right of way to turn left
You may turn left after stopping, if there is no traffic

questions.explanation: Flashing red arrow to the left: after stopping, you may turn if there is no traffic, yielding to pedestrians, oncoming traffic turning right and traffic from the right.
questions.manualRef: NaTIS Learner Driver Manual – Road Traffic Signs §8 Traffic signals (p.56)

questions.question: Which of these is, by definition, a "goods vehicle"? (Select all that apply.)
questions.explanation: Goods vehicles include truck-tractors, breakdown vehicles, converter dollies and adaptor dollies, but not motorcycles, motor cars, minibuses or buses.
questions.manualRef: NaTIS Learner Driver Manual – Rules of the Road – Acronyms and definitions (p.4)

questions.question: If a train is approaching and there is no stop line, stop no closer than ____ from the nearest rail.
questions.explanation: Railway crossing (W403/W404): stop no closer than 3 m from the nearest track, and not on the track or in the railway reserve.
questions.manualRef: NaTIS Learner Driver Manual – Road Traffic Signs §4.3 W403 (p.34)

questions.question: This sign means: "Two-way traffic crossroad ahead (one-way street crossed by a two-way street)".
questions.explanation: False. Combined curves (W211): two sharp curves in opposite directions, the first to the left. ("Two-way traffic crossroad ahead (one-way street crossed by a two-way street)" is the meaning of W213.)
questions.manualRef: NaTIS Learner Driver Manual – Road Traffic Signs §4.2 W211 (p.25)

questions.question: Goods on a vehicle must be safely contained in the body or securely fastened, and protected from being dislodged or spilled.
questions.explanation: Goods must be safely contained or securely fastened and properly protected from being dislodged or spilled.
questions.manualRef: NaTIS Learner Driver Manual – Rules of the Road §6.33 (p.25)

questions.question: What is the difference between an "intersection" and a "junction"?

options.text: A junction is the area within the intersection on the improved part of the road; an intersection includes sidewalks, verges, etc.
An intersection only exists where there are traffic lights
A junction includes the sidewalks, an intersection does not

questions.explanation: A junction is the area within the intersection on the improved part of the road. An intersection includes all parts of the road (sidewalks, verges, etc.).
questions.manualRef: NaTIS Learner Driver Manual – Rules of the Road – Acronyms and definitions (p.5)

questions.question: Which brake may also serve as the emergency brake on a light motor vehicle?
questions.explanation: The emergency brake and parking brake may be one and the same brake.
questions.manualRef: NaTIS Learner Driver Manual – Rules of the Road §6.14 (p.19)

questions.question: When may you take one hand off the steering wheel?

options.text: Whenever you are on a straight road
For gear changing, signalling or operating controls or devices
To rest your arm on the window

questions.explanation: Keep both hands on the steering wheel except for gear changing, signalling or operating controls or devices.
questions.manualRef: NaTIS K53 Light Motor Vehicle (Code B) manual, Module 14 (p.30)

questions.question: When overtaking a hazard on its right, you should obtain adequate clear space before returning to the left.
questions.explanation: Adequate clear space shall be obtained before returning.
questions.manualRef: NaTIS K53 Light Motor Vehicle (Code B) manual, Module 50 (p.71)

questions.question: Which signal takes precedence over all other traffic signals?
questions.explanation: Control hand signals (SS1): the traffic officer's signals take precedence over any other traffic signal.
questions.manualRef: NaTIS Learner Driver Manual – Road Traffic Signs §8.1 SS1 (p.57)

questions.question: From what age is a person regarded as an adult for seatbelt purposes, regardless of height?
questions.explanation: A child is a person between 3 and 14 years; a person older than 14 years is defined as an adult.
questions.manualRef: NaTIS Learner Driver Manual – Rules of the Road §6.17 (p.20)

questions.question: This sign means: "Speed limit 100 km/h".
questions.explanation: False. Overtaking prohibited (R214): do not overtake any vehicle for the next 500 m. ("Speed limit 100 km/h" is the meaning of R201.)
questions.manualRef: NaTIS Learner Driver Manual – Road Traffic Signs §3.3 R214 (p.12)

questions.question: In an emergency you may tow another motor vehicle (not a trailer) together with a trailer.
questions.explanation: In an emergency it is permitted to draw or tow one other motor vehicle, which is not a trailer, and a trailer.
questions.manualRef: NaTIS Learner Driver Manual – Rules of the Road §6.58 (p.36)

questions.question: What does "park" mean?

options.text: Bringing a vehicle to a standstill for any length of time
Stopping only when the engine is switched off
Keeping a vehicle stationary for longer than reasonably necessary to load or unload persons or goods

questions.explanation: "Park" means to keep a vehicle stationary for longer than reasonably necessary for loading or unloading persons or goods (not for causes beyond the driver's control).
questions.manualRef: NaTIS Learner Driver Manual – Rules of the Road – Acronyms and definitions (p.7)

questions.question: What is the "gross vehicle mass (GVM)" of a vehicle?

options.text: The maximum mass of the vehicle and its load as specified by the manufacturer
The mass of the load only
The mass of the vehicle plus fuel
The mass of the empty vehicle

questions.explanation: "GVM" means the maximum mass of the vehicle and its load as specified by the manufacturer (or determined by the registering authority).
questions.manualRef: NaTIS Learner Driver Manual – Rules of the Road – Acronyms and definitions (p.4)

questions.question: By definition, a "public road" includes the verge of the road.
questions.explanation: "Public road" includes the verge of any such road, street or thoroughfare, and bridges, ferries or drifts traversed by it.
questions.manualRef: NaTIS Learner Driver Manual – Rules of the Road – Acronyms and definitions (p.7)

questions.question: A load is carried on the roof of a motor car. How high may the load be?

options.text: Not more than the height of the car
There is no limit if it is tied down
Not more than half the height of the car

questions.explanation: Goods on a motor car roof may not exceed one-half of the height of the car (measured from the highest point of the roof).
questions.manualRef: NaTIS Learner Driver Manual – Rules of the Road §6.33 (p.25)

questions.question: Which sign means: "Two-way traffic ahead"?
questions.explanation: Two-way traffic (W212): the one-way roadway will soon become two-way.
questions.manualRef: NaTIS Learner Driver Manual – Road Traffic Signs §4.2 W212 (p.26)

questions.question: At an unguarded level crossing, a motorcyclist should cross…

options.text: Standing on the footpegs at high speed
As near to 90° to the rails as possible, without moving out of the lane
At a sharp angle to the rails

questions.explanation: The crossing should be executed as near to 90° as possible, without moving out of the lane.
questions.manualRef: NaTIS K53 Motor Cycles manual Part 2, Module 41 (p.58)

questions.question: How far may a load project beyond the rear end of a light motor vehicle?
questions.explanation: Goods may not project more than 1,8 m beyond the rear end of a light or heavy motor vehicle.
questions.manualRef: NaTIS Learner Driver Manual – Rules of the Road §6.35 (p.26)

questions.question: A vehicle may be used on a public road if exhaust smoke leaks into the passenger compartment, as long as the windows are open.
questions.explanation: A vehicle may not be used if exhaust gas or smoke leaks into the driving cab or passenger compartment.
questions.manualRef: NaTIS Learner Driver Manual – Rules of the Road §6.21 (p.22)

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Jetty edge or river bank ahead

questions.explanation: Jetty edge or river bank (W348).
questions.manualRef: NaTIS Learner Driver Manual – Road Traffic Signs §4.3 W348 (p.31)

questions.question: What does this sign indicate?

options.text: Staggered junction: side road from the right first, then from the left
Staggered junction: side road from the left first, then from the right
Side road junction from the right

questions.explanation: Skew T-junction (W105/W106): another road meets yours at an angle; slow down and be prepared to stop.
questions.manualRef: NaTIS Learner Driver Manual – Road Traffic Signs §4.1 W105 (p.23)

questions.question: What is the "tare" of a motor vehicle?

options.text: The maximum mass the vehicle may carry
The mass of the vehicle ready to travel, including the spare wheel and standard accessories, but excluding fuel
The mass of the vehicle with fuel and passengers
The mass of the vehicle with a full load

questions.explanation: "Tare" is the mass of the vehicle ready to travel on a road including spare wheel and standard equipment, but not fuel.
questions.manualRef: NaTIS Learner Driver Manual – Rules of the Road – Acronyms and definitions (p.8)

questions.question: The windscreen of a light motor vehicle must be made of safety glass.
questions.explanation: The windscreen must afford sufficient visibility, be of safety glass and have a visible light transmittance of at least 70%.
questions.manualRef: NaTIS Learner Driver Manual – Rules of the Road §6.19 (p.21)

questions.question: What does this sign indicate?

options.text: Agricultural vehicles may cross or enter the road
General warning: danger of some kind ahead
Domestic animals on the road (next 2 km)

questions.explanation: Domestic animals (W310–W312): free-ranging animals may be on the road for the next 2 km.
questions.manualRef: NaTIS Learner Driver Manual – Road Traffic Signs §4.3 W310 (p.27)
